Selected alloys were directionally solidified (DS) as cylindrical bars in ceramic cluster molds in a Bridgman furnace with a withdrawal rate of 200 mm/h. Prior to withdrawal, the charge alloys were induction melted and poured into the investment molds preheated to 1550 °C. Conventional helical starters were utilized to initiate single crystal growth.
All the heat treatments were performed in air in a high temperature tube furnace and followed by water quenching.
the initial phase to form during solidification was either the γ phase (FCC Ni-solid solution) or the δ phase (HCP Re-rich phase)
δ-Re nucleated at a temperature well above the liquidus temperature of pure Ni and grew unconstrained into six-fold Re-rich dendrites
the difference in the liquidus temperature was within 1 °C for five alloys and less than 1.7 °C for another alloy. This suggests that the accuracy of liquidus temperature in this study is ± 1 °C.

mechanisms.name: heterogeneous nucleation of gamma grains on delta dendrites

evidence.quote: These dendrites served as potent nucleation sites for γ grains as temperature decreased during directional solidification.

mechanisms.name: suppression of delta phase formation by Ru addition

evidence.quote: Ruthenium additions in the range of 2.5~9.0 at.% (4.1~14.1 wt.%) lowered the temperature at which the δ nucleated and eventually suppressed the formation of this phase during solidification.

To better understand the influence of Ru, Re and Al on single crystal solidification, three sets of alloys were examined: 1) alloy CM-C2, a Ru-free alloy containing high levels of Re and Al (1.7 and 18.5 at.%, respectively); 2) alloys CM-A3 and UM-F3
Selected alloys were directionally solidified (DS) as cylindrical bars in ceramic cluster molds in a Bridgman furnace with a withdrawal rate of 200 mm/h.
δ-Re nucleated at a temperature well above the liquidus temperature of pure Ni and grew unconstrained into six-fold Re-rich dendrites
These dendrites served as potent nucleation sites for γ grains as temperature decreased during directional solidification.
Ru additions also increased the liquidus temperatures of the multicomponent superalloys.
Ruthenium additions in the range of 2.5~9.0 at.% (4.1~14.1 wt.%) lowered the temperature at which the δ nucleated and eventually suppressed the formation of this phase during solidification.
